applicability.population_description: open ml430 mirrors stating a pure bitwise (land/lor/ldiff/xor) Nat equality with no existing cross-operator machinery in the tree (re-verified absent on every run of this compiler)

budget.estimate: one Nat.rec-free proof per target: 1 extensionality application + up to 3 rewrite chains + an 8-case split for a 3-variable identity, 4-case for 2 variables

falsifiable_prediction: Both ['F:ml430-nat-and-or-distrib-left-fe131f64', 'F:ml430-nat-and-or-distrib-right-0daaa284'] are closable by this exact 4-step recipe with no induction beyond the finite case split. This is wrong if the testBit rewrite chain fails to reach a closed arithmetic goal (e.g. if AxNat.mul/AxNat.ble do not reduce at the bound {0,1} values without further lemmas).

negative_controls.why_declines: same two-operator bitwise shape (lor n m = land n m) but mathematically FALSE (n=1,m=2: lor=3, land=0) -- a deliberate mutation. The recipe's finite case-split reaches a bit assignment where the two sides differ and correctly fails to close, rather than fabricating a proof.

top-level connective is Iff, not Eq -- the recipe's first step (Nat.eq_of_testbit_eq) does not even type-check against an Iff goal, so the shape predicate must exclude it rather than let the recipe fail late.

recipe: 1. Apply Nat.eq_of_testbit_eq to reduce the goal to 'forall i, lhs.testBit i = rhs.testBit i'. 2. Rewrite both sides to a Nat.testBit-headed normal form using testbit_land / testbit_lor / testbit_ldiff / testbit_xor. 3. Bound each testBit i term to {0,1} via testbit_le_one and case -split (finite exhaustion). 4. Each of the resulting closed arithmetic goals over {0,1} closes by evaluation.

shape.description: An equality between two Nat-valued expressions built purely from land/lor/ldiff/xor (no arithmetic mixed in), whose top-level connective is Eq, not Iff.

requires_all_of: only bitwise operators on both sides

validation_examples: F-nat-testbit-land, F-nat-testbit-lor, F-nat-eq-of-testbit-eq, F-nat-testbit-le-one are the proved kernel lemmas this recipe composes; none of them is new work
